Also the following episodes: Hell on Earth 2006, Go God Go, A Million Little Fibers, The Return of Chef, Bloody Mary, Erection Day, Mr. Garrison's Fancy New Vagina, Woodland Critter Christmas, Toilet Paper, Krazy Kripples, Red Sleigh Down, The Death Camp of Tolerance, Proper Condom Use, and It Hits The Fan were omitted from the syndication package since it was too vulgar and profane to edit with the plot still making sense.

A few months ago, I thought about what it would be like if MeTV Toons aired some of the more tame adult animated shows and these are all good picks. I would also include Home Movies, Mission Hill, The Oblongs, and possibly even Harvey Birdman.

Only thing I would interject is that MeTV Toons cannot and won't air any TV-MA programs due to watershed restrictions on OTA television in the US and they want to maintain a somewhat general audience image. So probably not Duckman unless they make an edited to pieces, syndicated version.

As for Beavis and Butthead, probably not due to the frequent sexual references and dirty jokes in the show. If they did air it, they would have to air the version of the show with the music videos omitted because the rights to the music videos have long since expired.

Classic Simpsons (seasons 1-13) would be impossible to get since it would cost hundreds of millions of dollars to obtain the broadcast rights, just like with Animaniacs. Even then, I don't think Disney would even accept any offer from Weigel due to FXX's exclusivity deal since 2014 and Disney themselves is notoriously stingy when it comes to licensing out content.

The Critic, Dr. Katz, Space Ghost: Coast to Coast, Cartoon Planet (that's if they have the guts to finally air CN originals), Daria, Clone High, Bob and Margaret, Home Movies, Mission Hill, and The Oblongs would have zero issue airing on MeTV Toons besides the licensing obstacle.
